<article class="prose"><h2>Start with a prediction</h2><p>Choose a layer and a unit. Look at its category responses, then inspect the individual words. Start with L12/U646, which strongly prefers animals. Find a unit that prefers plants and compare the two profiles.</p><p>The 20 original units were selected using a separate animal/tool vocabulary. The layer explorer also includes exploratory examples so you can visit every layer. Check the selection label before treating an example as part of the frozen set.</p><h2>What you are seeing</h2><p>These are saved measurements from a pretrained Gemma model. The controls choose which measurement to display. They do not run a new prompt, disable a neuron, or change the model’s answer. A strong category response is an observation to investigate, not proof that one unit stores a concept.</p><p><a class="button-link" href="/posts/looking-for-an-animal-neuron/">Read the experiment</a> <a class="text-link" href="/assets/neuron-playground/index.html">Open playground on its own</a> <a class="text-link" href="/assets/functional-localizer/evidence.json">Download evidence</a></p></article>
